edges.reason: Absolute value is defined as the distance from a point to the origin. That definition presupposes a number line with an origin and a unit length, which give distance its meaning.
edges.scope: geometric meaning of absolute value as distance to origin

edges.reason: The distance-from-origin definition refers to the point representing the number, so number-to-point interpretation is a component of this geometric criterion.
The target explicitly asks for the equal absolute values of opposite numbers; the opposite-number relation is part of that assertion.
edges.scope: Criterion: opposites have equal absolute values

edges.reason: The ellipse definition uses distances as segment lengths, which is a synthetic notion. The coordinate distance formula is needed only later, when deriving the equation.
edges.scope: later coordinate treatment of the definition

edges.reason: A circle is the limiting case where the two foci coincide and gives a useful contrast. The focal definition itself does not depend on the circle equation.
edges.scope: circle as contrast or limiting case

edges.reason: The definition sums two point-to-point distances. Why the constant must exceed the focal distance follows from the fact that the straight segment is the shortest path between two points.
edges.scope: distance meaning; constant exceeds focal distance

edges.reason: The ellipse definition gives a helpful analogy, swapping sum for difference. The hyperbola definition is still self-contained and can be learned directly.

edges.scope: absolute value of the distance difference

edges.reason: The hyperbola compares two point-to-point distances. The condition that the constant is less than the focal distance rests on the segment-shortest fact, through the triangle inequality.
edges.scope: distance meaning; constant less than focal distance
